title: Leadership sync quick prep — Jun 25 2025
body:
Purpose:
- Quick personal prep for weekly leadership sync. Capture things I need to surface, decisions to push for, and follow-ups to assign. Keep this terse so I can read in 5 min before standup.

Topline to say in the meeting:
- Hosted API growth steady; tail latency improvement from recent runtime kernel change (v1.14) — median down ~8ms on small models, p95 down ~45ms for 4k seq.
- Dedicated capacity usage: 78% committed, 12% burst used last week; billing anomaly flagged for two customers (see linked JIRA).
- Private pipeline: closed one PoC for healthcare; next steps around KMS integration and audit logs.

Agenda items I want on the table (5–10 min each):
1) SLA bump ask for Dedicated tier — propose 99.9 -> 99.95 for reserved customers (ops should confirm impact on SRE load).
2) Rollout policy for fallback models — ask for greenlight on auto-fallback to quantized variants when cross-region capacity saturates.
3) Quick readout on Optimize recommendations pilot — early wins and unit-cost delta.

Quick numbers to cite (have to memorize these):
- Hosted: 4.2B tokens/day; cost per 1M tokens (weighted) = $7.8 after rebates.
- Dedicated: avg latency per request = 120ms (small), 310ms (long); capacity saturation peaks at 15:00 PST.
- Private: 3 active pilots; 2 pending compliance signoffs.

Key asks / decisions we need from leadership this week:
- Approve limited SLA increase for Dedicated (risk: higher on-call/credits). Decision due Fri 6/27 so sales can update proposals.
- Approve $150k runway reallocation to accelerate KMS/HSM certifications for Private (need exec sign-off for vendor contract).
- Confirm product stance on auto-fallback: permissive default + opt-out for enterprise customers.

Questions to raise (short):
- To CTO: how aggressive on kernel/FP16 changes for hosted models before Q3 launch? Do we accept transient regressions in a canary?
- To CRO: are we comfortable communicating a tentative SLA increase to prospects before engineering finalizes impact?
- To Head of SRE: what on-call capacity is needed if SLA increases (ballpark FTE)?

Risks / things to call out quickly:
- If we push SLA without more aggressive autoscaling, we may need to offer larger credits on outages — need risk budget number.
- Fallback to quantized models may increase hallucination risk on certain tasks (ops/research should define guardrails).
- Billing anomaly with two customers may be symptomatic of meter mismatch for multi-model routing — investigate before customer escalates.

Notes-to-self (what to say):
- Start with quick wins: latency numbers and Dedicated utilization to frame ask.
- Then the decision asks (SLA + KMS $). Keep ask specific: timeline and budget.
- End with one data point from Optimize pilot showing unit cost reduction (makes the cost-savings argument tangible).

Action items to assign in the meeting (draft list):
- SRE: produce a 1-pager impact estimate for SLA increase (owner: Lena Ortiz, due: 2025-06-27).
- Finance: model credit exposure for 99.95 SLA across top 20 customers (owner: Arjun Patel, due: 2025-06-30).
- Product/Infra: draft fallback policy + opt-out API for enterprise (owner: Sophie Kramer, due: 2025-07-03).
- Security: vendor evaluation and cost estimate for HSM/KMS acceleration (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2025-07-02).
- Billing: verify meter definitions and reconcile the two anomalous customers, escalate if mismatch (owner: Priya Singh, ASAP, update by 2025-06-26).

Parking lot (don't bring up unless asked):
- Consider temporary credits for customers in burst windows while we tune autoscaling.
- Potentially push a communication to customers about upcoming improvements to latency and rollout policies.

Draft one-liner I can read to open the topic: "Hosted performance is trending better after the runtime kernel changes; we have a narrow window to improve SLA and go-to-market messaging for Dedicated customers — need leadership sign-off on two items today: SLA bump runway and accelerating KMS certifications for Private."

Personal scratch notes (raw):
- Call Alex before meeting re: sales pipeline sensitivity to SLA changes.
- Remind SRE that increasing SLA might need both autoscaling config and more aggressive fallbacks (auto-fallback to q4-bit models).
- Keep the $ ask framed as reallocation from Ops discretionary, not new headcount (easier to push in exec).

Follow-ups after meeting (my checklist):
- Send meeting notes + assigned actions with owners and dates (template email).
- Ping Lena for the SRE 1-pager draft; if not in 48h escalate to CTO.
- Confirm Arjun's finance model and get a single slide showing expected credit exposure worst-case.
- Add fallback policy doc to product backlog and link to rollout PR (I will create ticket).

Tone reminders: short, confident, data-first. If there's pushback ask for a specific concern and convert to an action item (don’t get bogged in long debates).

End.
